# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.

        id: ratchet

          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi

# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

CRAP targets — bring each named function under 30. Strategies:

1. `postTestAutomationResults.js::publishExistingBranch` (49.5): CC=7, cov≈7%. Extract a pure `decidePublishStrategy(localSha, remoteSha, mergeBase)` returning 'up-to-date' | 'fast-forward' | 'adopt-remote' | 'diverged', then the function becomes a thin runner. Adding characterization tests for the git command sequences raises coverage. CC of publishExistingBranch after extraction: sequence of if/try. New helpers must be ≤8 CRAP (cover them or CC≤2). `decidePublishStrategy` has CC ~4-5 → needs tests. But helpers module postTestAutomationResultsHelpers.js is already fully tested. I could add decidePublishStrategy there and test it.

Actually, wait — the deeper question: how does coverage get measured? The tests eval-load modules; publishExistingBranch is called within performGitOperations in the noNewCommit path — only one branch. To get coverage of publishExistingBranch up, existing test "pushes synced existing branch..." hits it with localSha=='? Let's see: in that test, git rev-parse HEAD returns '' (default '), so localSha=' → skips to final push branch. So one path covered.

Simplest path to CRAP ≤30 for CC=7: CRAP = 49(1-cov)² + 7 ≤ 30 → (1-cov)² ≤ 23/49 → 1-cov ≤ 0.685 → cov ≥ 31.5%. So covering ~32% of branches suffices. Extracting decidePublishStrategy (CC≈5) with full test coverage removes decision complexity from the runner too.

Let me compute actual CC by running crap4js on the coverage output. Wait for the background job.

2. `checkBugTestsPassed.js::action` (44.5): CC? 44.5 = CC²(1-cov)²+CC. CC=6: 36(1-cov)²+6=44.5 → (1-cov)²=1.07 impossible. CC=7: 49(1-cov)²+7=44.5 → (1-cov)²=0.765 → cov≈12.5%. Existing tests cover the action. Plan: extract pure helpers — the big `isBlockingTC` and branch clusters (rework/blocked comments building) into a helpers module + tests. Actually findDirectLinkedTCs (15.8) and isBlockingTC (11) are nested functions defined inside action — they count as separate functions already but they're nested... they appear in baseline. Extracting the comment-building (buildBlockingComment etc.) to a pure helper module with tests reduces CC of action and adds covered functions.

3. `publishDiscoveryToConfluence.js::action` (42.2): CC=6 → 36(1-cov)²+6=42.2 → (1-cov)²=1.005 impossible. CC=7? 49x²+7=42.2→x²=0.718→cov≈15%. 

4. `fetchConfluenceOutputContext.js::action` (45.6): similar.

Common approach for all: extract pure helpers into existing/new helper modules, move them top level (out of action), add unit tests covering helpers + more action branches.

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"
          OUT="$RUNNER_TEMP/baseline-out/$BASELINE_ASSET"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"

          "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold 99999 > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap-all.txt" || true
          if [ "${{ steps.baseline.outputs.present }}" = "true" ]; then
            cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" "$OUT"
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --update-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
            sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            if cmp -s "$OUT" "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET"; then
              echo "baseline unchanged — nothing to upload (marker refreshed)"
              gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
              exit 0

          fi
          tail -1 "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          if gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" >/dev/null 2>&1; then

#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#

#

name: Quality

on:

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"
          OUT="$RUNNER_TEMP/baseline-out/$BASELINE_ASSET"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"
          # Full report (every function) for the README badges; ratchet steps keep their own outputs.
          "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold 99999 > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap-all.txt" || true
          if [ "${{ steps.baseline.outputs.present }}" = "true" ]; then
            cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" "$OUT"
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --update-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
            sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            if cmp -s "$OUT" "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET"; then
              echo "baseline unchanged — nothing to upload (marker refreshed)"
              gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
              exit 0
            fi
          else
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --write-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          fi
          tail -1 "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          if gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            gh release upload "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --clobber
          else
            gh release create "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --prerelease --latest=false \
              --title "CRAP baseline (rolling)" \
              --notes "Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release."
          fi
          # Marker the 'gate' job reads to skip runs when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
          gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
          echo "baseline released: $(node -e "const b=require('$OUT');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"
          OUT="$RUNNER_TEMP/baseline-out/$BASELINE_ASSET"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"
          # Full report (every function) for the README badges; ratchet steps keep their own outputs.
          "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold 99999 > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap-all.txt" || true
          if [ "${{ steps.baseline.outputs.present }}" = "true" ]; then
            cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" "$OUT"
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --update-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
            sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            if cmp -s "$OUT" "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET"; then
              echo "baseline unchanged — nothing to upload (marker refreshed)"
              gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
              exit 0

          else

          fi
          tail -1 "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          if gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" >/dev/null 2>&1; then

Actually, wait — the deeper question: how does coverage get measured? Let's see: in that test, git rev-parse HEAD returns '' (default '), so localSha=' → skips to final push branch. So one path covered.

          else

            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"
          OUT="$RUNNER_TEMP/baseline-out/$BASELINE_ASSET"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"
          # Full report (every function) for the README badges; ratchet steps keep their own outputs.
          "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold 99999 > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap-all.txt" || true
          if [ "${{ steps.baseline.outputs.present }}" = "true" ]; then
            cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" "$OUT"
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \

            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"
          OUT="$RUNNER_TEMP/baseline-out/$BASELINE_ASSET"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"

          "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold 99999 > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap-all.txt" || true
          if [ "${{ steps.baseline.outputs.present }}" = "true" ]; then
            cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" "$OUT"
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \

            sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            if cmp -s "$OUT" "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET"; then

              gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
              exit 0

          fi
          tail -1 "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          if gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" >/dev/null 2>&1; then

        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e

          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \

            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)

          set -e

          else

            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"
          OUT="$RUNNER_TEMP/baseline-out/$BASELINE_ASSET"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"
          # Full report (every function) for the README badges; ratchet steps keep their own outputs.
          "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold 99999 > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap-all.txt" || true
          if [ "${{ steps.baseline.outputs.present }}" = "true" ]; then
            cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" "$OUT"
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --update-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
            sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            if cmp -s "$OUT" "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET"; then
              echo "baseline unchanged — nothing to upload (marker refreshed)"
              gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
              exit 0
            fi
          else
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --write-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          fi
          tail -1 "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          if gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            gh release upload "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --clobber
          else
            gh release create "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --prerelease --latest=false \
              --title "CRAP baseline (rolling)" \
              --notes "Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release."
          fi
          # Marker the 'gate' job reads to skip runs when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
          gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
          echo "baseline released: $(node -e "const b=require('$OUT');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      - name: Publish README badges (main only — data lives on the 'badges' branch)

          set -e

          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"

          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)

          set -e

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet

          set +e

In the shared version, `isAheadOfRemote('', '', 'x')` → `!!(' && ...)` → false → 'diverged' → pushBranchWithLease — normal push then force-with-lease. Original in that scenario: ff push attempt then falls through to same escalation — identical commands, except the original logs 'Fast-forward push failed:' on failure instead of 'Normal push failed...' — wait no: original: ff push fails → warn 'Fast-forward push failed:' → falls through → normal push → fail → 'Normal push failed, retrying with --force-with-lease...'. So original does push, push, lease; shared does push, lease. Different command sequence! So I CANOT reuse the shared module's publishExistingBranch verbatim for postTestAutomationResults — behaviour (command sequence) would change in the edge case where remoteSha is empty.

Hmm wait, in postTestAutomationResults' original: when would remoteSha be ''? revParse catches failure → ''. And mergeBase is only computed when both local & remote non-empty; otherwise mergeBase='. So scenario: localSha='abc', remoteSha=' → mergeBase='. Condition: mergeBase===remoteSha ('==') true; mergeBase!==localSha ('!=='abc') true → ff branch → push. So yes: original pushes (with "ff" semantics) then on failure falls through to normal push + lease. Also scenario localSha=' remoteSha=': same → ff push attempt.

To keep the exact command order, I'll extract pure decision helpers in postTestAutomationResults.js matching the ORIGINAL conditions exactly:

```js
function decidePublishStrategy(localSha, remoteSha, mergeBase) {
   if (localSha && remoteSha && localSha === remoteSha) return 'identical';
   if (mergeBase === remoteSha && mergeBase !== localSha) return 'ahead';
   if (mergeBase === localSha && mergeBase !== remoteSha) return 'behind';
   return 'diverged';
}
```

Original computes mergeBase only when local&&remote. Command order: fetch, rev-parse HEAD, rev-parse origin/branch, [merge-base if both], then decisions. Preserve.

          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"
          OUT="$RUNNER_TEMP/baseline-out/$BASELINE_ASSET"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"
          # Full report (every function) for the README badges; ratchet steps keep their own outputs.
          "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold 99999 > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap-all.txt" || true
          if [ "${{ steps.baseline.outputs.present }}" = "true" ]; then
            cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" "$OUT"
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --update-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
            sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            if cmp -s "$OUT" "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET"; then
              echo "baseline unchanged — nothing to upload (marker refreshed)"
              gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
              exit 0
            fi
          else
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --write-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          fi
          tail -1 "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          if gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            gh release upload "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --clobber
          else
            gh release create "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --prerelease --latest=false \
              --title "CRAP baseline (rolling)" \
              --notes "Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release."

          else

          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"
          OUT="$RUNNER_TEMP/baseline-out/$BASELINE_ASSET"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"
          # Full report (every function) for the README badges; ratchet steps keep their own outputs.
          "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold 99999 > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap-all.txt" || true
          if [ "${{ steps.baseline.outputs.present }}" = "true" ]; then
            cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" "$OUT"
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --update-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
            sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            if cmp -s "$OUT" "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET"; then
              echo "baseline unchanged — nothing to upload (marker refreshed)"
              gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
              exit 0
            fi
          else
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --write-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          fi
          tail -1 "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          if gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            gh release upload "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --clobber
          else

/**
 * Publish Discovery To Confluence — postJSAction for the discovery agent.
 *
 * Reads outputs/discovery/ (a Markdown folder written by the CLI agent per
 * instructions/discovery/output_rules.md) and syncs it to a Confluence page
 * tree anchored under a per-project parent page:

 *     either is missing, skip publishing and post a Jira comment explaining
 *     what to configure — this keeps the agent itself fully generic.
 *  2. Find-or-create the ticket's own Confluence page (title
 *     "<ticketKey> <ticket summary>") as a child of parentPageId. Matched by
 *     ticket-key PREFIX (not exact title) so a later summary edit doesn't
 *     create a duplicate page.
 *  3. Sync outputs/discovery/ under that page via
 *     confluence_sync_markdown_directory (index.md becomes the page's own
 *     body; every other .md file becomes a child page).
 *  4. Post replies to any inline comments the CLI agent directly addressed
 *     (outputs/confluence_replies.json — same mechanism as
 *     story_solution/story_description, see contentOutput.js), using
 *     confluence_reply_to_inline_comment via
 *     contentOutput.publishCommentReplies().
 *  5. Post a Jira comment linking to the page, plus the usual token-usage
 *     comment.
 */

/**
 * Publish Discovery To Confluence — postJSAction for the discovery agent.
 *
 * Reads outputs/discovery/ (a Markdown folder written by the CLI agent per
 * instructions/discovery/output_rules.md) and syncs it to a Confluence page
 * tree anchored under a per-project parent page:
 *
 *  1. Resolve discovery.space / discovery.parentPageId from project config
 *     (.dmtools/config.js — see js/configLoader.js DEFAULTS.discovery). If
 *     either is missing, skip publishing and post a Jira comment explaining
 *     what to configure — this keeps the agent itself fully generic.
 *  2. Find-or-create the ticket's own Confluence page (title
 *     "<ticketKey> <ticket summary>") as a child of parentPageId. Matched by
 *     ticket-key PREFIX (not exact title) so a later summary edit doesn't
 *     create a duplicate page.
 *  3. Sync outputs/discovery/ under that page via
 *     confluence_sync_markdown_directory (index.md becomes the page's own
 *     body; every other .md file becomes a child page).
 *  4. Post replies to any inline comments the CLI agent directly addressed
 *     (outputs/confluence_replies.json — same mechanism as
 *     story_solution/story_description, see contentOutput.js), using
 *     confluence_reply_to_inline_comment via
 *     contentOutput.publishCommentReplies().
 *  5. Post a Jira comment linking to the page, plus the usual token-usage
 *     comment.
 */

/**
 * Publish Discovery To Confluence — postJSAction for the discovery agent.
 *
 * Reads outputs/discovery/ (a Markdown folder written by the CLI agent per
 * instructions/discovery/output_rules.md) and syncs it to a Confluence page
 * tree anchored under a per-project parent page:
 *
 *  1. Resolve discovery.space / discovery.parentPageId from project config
 *     (.dmtools/config.js — see js/configLoader.js DEFAULTS.discovery). If
 *     either is missing, skip publishing and post a Jira comment explaining
 *     what to configure — this keeps the agent itself fully generic.
 *  2. Find-or-create the ticket's own Confluence page (title
 *     "<ticketKey> <ticket summary>") as a child of parentPageId. Matched by
 *     ticket-key PREFIX (not exact title) so a later summary edit doesn't
 *     create a duplicate page.
 *  3. Sync outputs/discovery/ under that page via

 *     confluence_reply_to_inline_comment via
 *     contentOutput.publishCommentReplies().
 *  5. Post a Jira comment linking to the page, plus the usual token-usage

 */

 *  3. Sync outputs/discovery/ under that page via

/**
 * Publish Discovery To Confluence — postJSAction for the discovery agent.
 *
 * Reads outputs/discovery/ (a Markdown folder written by the CLI agent per
 * instructions/discovery/output_rules.md) and syncs it to a Confluence page
 * tree anchored under a per-project parent page:
 *
 *  1. Resolve discovery.space / discovery.parentPageId from project config
 *     (.dmtools/config.js — see js/configLoader.js DEFAULTS.discovery). If
 *     either is missing, skip publishing and post a Jira comment explaining
 *     what to configure — this keeps the agent itself fully generic.
 *  2. Find-or-create the ticket's own Confluence page (title
 *     "<ticketKey> <ticket summary>") as a child of parentPageId. Matched by
 *     ticket-key PREFIX (not exact title) so a later summary edit doesn't
 *     create a duplicate page.
 *  3. Sync outputs/discovery/ under that page via
 *     confluence_sync_markdown_directory (index.md becomes the page's own
 *     body; every other .md file becomes a child page).
 *  4. Post replies to any inline comments the CLI agent directly addressed
 *     (outputs/confluence_replies.json — same mechanism as
 *     story_solution/story_description, see contentOutput.js), using
 *     confluence_reply_to_inline_comment via
 *     contentOutput.publishCommentReplies().
 *  5. Post a Jira comment linking to the page, plus the usual token-usage
 *     comment.
 */

/**
 * Publish Discovery To Confluence — postJSAction for the discovery agent.
 *
 * Reads outputs/discovery/ (a Markdown folder written by the CLI agent per
 * instructions/discovery/output_rules.md) and syncs it to a Confluence page
 * tree anchored under a per-project parent page:
 *
 *  1. Resolve discovery.space / discovery.parentPageId from project config
 *     (.dmtools/config.js — see js/configLoader.js DEFAULTS.discovery). If
 *     either is missing, skip publishing and post a Jira comment explaining
 *     what to configure — this keeps the agent itself fully generic.
 *  2. Find-or-create the ticket's own Confluence page (title
 *     "<ticketKey> <ticket summary>") as a child of parentPageId. Matched by
 *     ticket-key PREFIX (not exact title) so a later summary edit doesn't
 *     create a duplicate page.
 *  3. Sync outputs/discovery/ under that page via
 *     confluence_sync_markdown_directory (index.md becomes the page's own
 *     body; every other .md file becomes a child page).
 *  4. Post replies to any inline comments the CLI agent directly addressed

 *     story_solution/story_description, see contentOutput.js), using
 *     confluence_reply_to_inline_comment via
 *     contentOutput.publishCommentReplies().
 *  5. Post a Jira comment linking to the page, plus the usual token-usage
 *     comment.
 */

/**
 * Publish Discovery To Confluence — postJSAction for the discovery agent.
 *
 * Reads outputs/discovery/ (a Markdown folder written by the CLI agent per
 * instructions/discovery/output_rules.md) and syncs it to a Confluence page
 * tree anchored under a per-project parent page:
 *
 *  1. Resolve discovery.space / discovery.parentPageId from project config
 *     (.dmtools/config.js — see js/configLoader.js DEFAULTS.discovery). If
 *     either is missing, skip publishing and post a Jira comment explaining
 *     what to configure — this keeps the agent itself fully generic.
 *  2. Find-or-create the ticket's own Confluence page (title
 *     "<ticketKey> <ticket summary>") as a child of parentPageId. Matched by
 *     ticket-key PREFIX (not exact title) so a later summary edit doesn't
 *     create a duplicate page.
 *  3. Sync outputs/discovery/ under that page via
 *     confluence_sync_markdown_directory (index.md becomes the page's own
 *     body; every other .md file becomes a child page).
 *  4. Post replies to any inline comments the CLI agent directly addressed
 *     (outputs/confluence_replies.json — same mechanism as
 *     story_solution/story_description, see contentOutput.js), using
 *     confluence_reply_to_inline_comment via
 *     contentOutput.publishCommentReplies().
 *  5. Post a Jira comment linking to the page, plus the usual token-usage
 *     comment.
 */
